clue.text: Potable liquid on the wagon?

definitions.meaning: something fit to drink that comes from the tap
a teetotaller 'on the wagon' takes only the non-alcoholic stuff

explanation.surface: Someone who has given up alcohol sticks to soft drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap water is the potable liquid, and the phrase also describes what an abstainer is reduced to drinking.

clue.text: On who's inclined to take one?

definitions.text: On who's inclined to take one

parts.words: On who's inclined to take one
parts.note: read as a person keen to sign up newcomers, the 'one' taken being a new member of staff or a soldier

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to accept an offer of a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who enlists people for an army or firm takes on new hires one at a time.

clue.text: Approaches bridge partnership, securing attention

indicators.note: securing means the bridge pair holds the other piece fast between its letters

parts.note: North and South form one partnership at the bridge table
to lend an ear is to give attention

explanation.surface: A bridge pair gets near to winning while keeping everyone's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Securing' puts EAR inside NS.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw nearer to something is to approach it.

clue.text: Thankless recipient tearing off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of tearing have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An ungrateful person rips the present open and storms away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' signals an anagram of TEARING.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person shows no thanks for what has been received.

clue.text: Government permits capital punishment

parts.note: permits as a verb means lets or allows

explanation.surface: The state authorises the death penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: The scaffold for hanging stands by metonymy for execution itself.

clue.text: If orator falters one's on even firmer ground

indicators.note: a faltering speaker stumbles, so the letters stumble into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A speaker who stumbles ironically strengthens an opponent's case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falters' signals an anagram of IFORATOR, giving AFORTIOR; one's I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin logical phrase means 'with stronger reason', used when an argument holds all the more firmly.

clue.text: Second of defendants to be given fine in Surrey town

indicators.note: second of means take the second letter of the following word

parts.note: fine as in 'I'm fine' means well

explanation.surface: A Surrey magistrates' court fines one of the accused.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south-west of London; the town sits near Epsom. 'Second of' picks the E of defendants.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a small town in the county, near Epsom.

clue.text: Grey in places? Sailor will meet with shower

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor
with means together with, and
one that showers, as a pepper pot sprinkles or a gunner peppers a target

explanation.surface: A sailor meets a rain shower on a dull grey day.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair speckled with white among dark strands is grizzled in patches.

clue.text: Ready for the old parrot-cry?

definitions.meaning: ready means cash (the readies), here coins of times past
the squawk of Long John Silver's parrot in Treasure Island

explanation.surface: Someone prepared for the old bird's familiar squawk.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish silver dollars were old coinage, and Stevenson's pirate parrot screeches the phrase.

clue.text: Republican reform in Alabama port

indicators.note: in places the Republican and the reform inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama
to reform is to change

explanation.surface: A Republican pushes reform in the Deep South.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the Russian White Sea port, often spelt Arkhangelsk.
explanation.definitionFit: This northern Russian city is a seaport on the Dvina estuary.

clue.text: Printers' marks withdrawn from juvenile books

indicators.note: withdrawn says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some typographical symbols are pulled from children's books.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters ILEBO run across 'juvenile books'; 'withdrawn' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: These dagger-like or division-sign symbols are typographic marks used by printers and editors.

clue.text: Support for transactions on American ship

parts.note: Tr. is an abbreviation for transactions, as in the journals of learned societies
USS, United States Ship, prefixes the names of American naval vessels

explanation.surface: Backing for trade deals involving a US vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A framework of beams or a surgical belt gives support.

clue.text: For instance, Peter's flying as co-pilot

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters taking off and landing in a new order

explanation.surface: St Peter takes the controls as second pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' signals an anagram of ASCOPILOT. The definition reads 'Peter's' as 'belonging to, say, Peter', an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter was one of the twelve disciples, so things of his relate to an apostle.

clue.text: Treating bananas without good fertiliser

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild
without means leave out the letter for good

explanation.surface: Treating a banana plantation without good fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' drops the G of TREATING and 'bananas' scrambles what is left, TREATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Salts of nitric acid are widely spread on fields as plant food.

clue.text: Unknown writer's penned perfect piece about American war leader

indicators.note: penned means the author's name encloses the rest like a pen holding sheep

parts.note: Anon, short for anonymous, signs work whose author is unknown

indicators.note: about means the gem goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: a gem is a perfect example, a jewel

explanation.surface: An anonymous author writes a flawless piece about an American general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts AM inside GEM to make GAMEM; 'penned' puts that inside ANON.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend he was the king who commanded the Greek forces at Troy.

clue.text: Challenges with vessel found around College formerly?

indicators.note: found around means the ship's letters are placed on either side

parts.note: SS, steamship, prefixes a vessel's name
once means formerly

explanation.surface: Drinking challenges were issued with a cup at college in times past.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford a sconce was a forfeit, often downing a tankard of ale, for a breach of hall etiquette, hence the question mark. 'Found around' puts C plus ONCE inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford, to sconce someone was to challenge them to drink a penalty for a breach of manners.

clue.text: It pays to consult a professional

definitions.text: It pays to consult a professional

parts.words: It pays to consult a professional
parts.note: read not as advice but literally: the body of people who pay fees to see a lawyer or adviser

explanation.surface: Proverbial advice to seek expert help.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional's customers collectively are those who pay for advice.

clue.text: Unusual sapphire one lost, maybe

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of the gem are arranged in an unusual way
lost says a letter for one goes missing

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone has lost a rare sapphire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' drops one I from SAPPHIRE and 'Unusual' scrambles what is left, SAPPHRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps and maybe are interchangeable adverbs of possibility.

clue.text: Bit of news -money's raised to hold course in Oxford

indicators.note: to hold means the reversed letters enclose the course
raised in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: tin is slang for money, with the 's adding an S
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, a famous Oxford degree

explanation.surface: Newspaper item about higher fees for an Oxford degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns TINS into SNIT; 'to hold' puts PPE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A short extract or titbit of information is a small piece.

clue.text: Court officer has trouble getting into buffet

indicators.note: getting into means the trouble enters the blow

parts.note: to buffet is to strike, to biff
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: An official runs into difficulty at the buffet table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' tempts as the food spread; it is the verb, a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: This officer of a sheriff or court serves writs and seizes goods.

clue.text: Corby

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Corby (7)': the place name alone gives no wordplay or definition that builds the answer, so it looks cut short or garbled; no scan, and a quoted search finds no fuller version.

clue.text: What's behind advertisement seen around SA resort?

indicators.note: seen around means the advert wraps round the resort

parts.note: a poster is a printed advertisement
Rio de Janeiro is a South American resort city

explanation.surface: A billboard advertises a Brazilian beach resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen around' puts RIO inside POSTER, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rear or behind, as a noun, is a jocular word for the bottom.

clue.text: Seat occupied by Independent in Balkan capital

indicators.note: occupied by means the seat holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a sofa is an upholstered seat

explanation.surface: A seat is taken by an independent politician in a Balkan city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupied by' puts I inside SOFA.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Bulgaria, in the Balkans.

clue.text: Source of tablets found lying about in Aleutian Islands

indicators.note: lying about says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Medicine found strewn about remote Alaskan islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tablets' suggests pills; they are the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments. IANIS runs across the island name and 'lying about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses received the Commandments on stone on this mountain, per the Bible.

clue.text: Dance is attended by a bachelor in Morocco

parts.note: is shortened to 's gives S

indicators.note: in puts the bachelor inside the country code

parts.note: MA is the international code for Morocco

explanation.surface: A single man goes dancing in Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts B inside MA.
explanation.definitionFit: This lively Brazilian dance is a ballroom favourite.

clue.text: Mischievous fellow seen in river around here

indicators.note: seen in places the fellow within the reversed river
around means the river's name is turned back to front

parts.note: the Nile is the great river of Egypt

explanation.surface: A rascal is spotted in the local river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' turns NILE into ELIN and 'seen in' puts F inside it; 'here' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are impish sprites, so elf-like behaviour is impish and playful.

clue.text: Hospital number given by married bird in pub-that's capital

indicators.note: in places the run of pieces inside the pub's letters

parts.note: PH stands for public house
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Hospital staff and a married woman meet in a pub in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital of Cambodia. 'In' puts HNOMPEN inside PH.
explanation.definitionFit: This city on the Mekong is Cambodia's seat of government.

clue.text: Shady campsite agent offering video recordings, maybe?

indicators.note: shady means dodgy, so the letters are crooked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dodgy campsite agent sells videotapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shady' signals an anagram of CAMPSITE AGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Video cassettes and audio reels store recordings on magnetised strips.
